title: Launch slate negotiation and resource ledger for runtime/console/api launches
creator: Maya Singh
description: Create a structured ‘resource ledger’ and negotiation cadence to coordinate simultaneous launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces. The ledger is a single source of truth for capacity reservations (Dedicated pools, burst lanes, region quotas), launch windows, and OKR mappings so Product, Eng, and Platform SREs can adjudicate conflicts without ad-hoc email threads. Deliverables: (1) ledger schema and process, (2) negotiation cadence + arbitration rules, (3) tooling prototype (spreadsheet -> lightweight web view + API), and (4) acceptance criteria and runbook for committing/rolling back reservations.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger schema capturing team, feature, capacity units, region, window, and contingency lanes defined and approved by Eng and SRE
Negotiation cadence documented: weekly interlock + 72-hour finalization window before launch cutoff
Prototype ledger view (Google Sheet + read-only web preview) with sample runtime/console/api entries for two concurrent launches
Arbitration rules that cover overcommit, preemption, and emergency escalation documented and ratified by PM/ENG leads
End-to-end test: schedule two mock launches that would conflict; use ledger to resolve and produce deployment plan with fallbacks
timeline: 2026-03-10: Ticket created and kickoff with PM, Platform SRE, Runtime lead
2026-03-18: Negotiation cadence proposal due (weekly interlock + finalization rules)
2026-03-24: Prototype ledger populated with Q2 planned launches for validation
2026-04-01: Arbitration playbook and escalation contacts finalized
2026-04-10: Runbook and handoff to Launch Ops; mock conflict rehearsal
risks: Over-allocating Dedicated/GPU pools to low-priority launches causing capacity cliffs
Teams bypassing ledger and creating shadow reservations (people/process risk)
Insufficient telemetry to validate actual capacity usage post-launch
Arbitration rules ambiguous leading to late escalations and missed windows
notes: 2026-03-11: Quick sync NOTES - Runtime team proposed reserving 20% burst capacity per regional pool for emergency fixes; Platform SRE asked for more concrete usage metrics (link to dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/region-capacity)
2026-03-12: Shared initial ledger schema on Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LAUNCH/Resource+Ledger+Draft. Feedback requested from Console PMs and Pricing team.

2026-03-13: Decision: finalization window set to 72 hours before the launch cutoff. Rationale: reduces last-minute surprises while preserving agility for critical patches. Action: update runbook and sprint calendar interlock.

2026-03-14: Prototype prototype-url (Google Sheet): https://drive.google.com/sheet/proto-launch-ledger (read-only). Populated with two examples: runtime:session-cache-eviction (Q2 week 2) and console:rollout-flag-refactor (Q2 week 2). Noted conflict on GPU reservations for region-us-west-2.

2026-03-14: Follow-ups - Owen to coordinate a triage meeting (2026-03-16) with Runtime, Dedicated infra, and Pricing to agree on capacity accounting unit (CU) conversion table. GitHub PR template proposed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-ops/pulls (PR: #342).

Decision log: reserve 'contingency lanes' that are pre-authorized but billable to a shared ops pool; rights to preempt belong to Launch Ops during declared blackout windows. This was approved by Platform SRE on 2026-03-14.

Open question: integrate ledger with Console 'launch timeline' UI vs keep ledger as canonical source and build read-only mirrors. Trade-off: speed to value (sheet + web preview) vs long-term single-source integration cost. Recommended: MVP sheet + lightweight web preview; roadmap item to integrate in console-2026.2
